full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the order of conviction and sentence under section 379 BPC passed by Mr. S.U. Chowdhury Magistrate, 1st Class Sadar South, Comilla in G.R. Case No. 1082/69. The learned Magistrate sentenced the petitioner to pay a fine of Rs. 500/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 months. 

 The prosecution case in short was that the complainant Abdul Jabbar purchased the truck bearing No. Comilla T. 627 from the accused Syed Ali Sardar for Rs. 9,000/-. The truck was purchased on 1.469 and since then the complainant was in possession of the truck. On 9.11.69 the case truck was sent to Brahmanbaria on hire when the accused dishonestly took away the said truck from the possession of the driver Sandu Mia and assistant Taru Mia The complainant filed an ejher in the Kotwali Police on 27.11.69. Thereafter the Police submitted the charge sheet against the accused under section 379 B.P.C. The prosecution examined 8 witnesses and the defence examined 4 witnesses. The defence case was that the case truck was never sold to the complainant. It was let out on hire to the complainant on 2-6-69 with a condition that the complainant would pay Rs. 400/- per month to the accused as 'bhara' of the truck. The complainant neither paid the 'bhara' nor handed back the truck to the accused and therefore, the accused took back the truck in his possession. In order to grab the truck and to avoid the payment of the accumulated rental dues the complainant brought this false case. 

 3. On consideration of evidence the learned Magistrate disbelieved the defence case and found the accused guilty for taking away the truck from the possession of the complainant without his consent with a dishonest intention and thereby committed the offence under section 379 B. P C. 

 5. Mr Mozibur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner contended that the Courts below proceeded on a wrong assumption and pointed out that the court below gave stress to the defence case in order to bring out whether the defence could substantiate its plea thereby altering the nature of onus as required in Criminal Law. Thy learned Advocate pointed out that the court below completely overlooked the fact that the blue book and the road permit both stood in the name of the accused petitioner which clearly demonstrate that the petitioner had not been divested of the ownership of the truck. Further finding of the Court below that even assuming the truck was in possession of the complainant of the basis of Mara, as claimed by the accused that the accused had no right to snatch away the truck is unwarranted. 

 6. Mr. Mozibur Rahman pointedly drew the attention of the Court that section 91 of the Evidence Act precludes any interpretation by oral evidence of Ext. A. If Exhibit A remains unassailed the falsity of the prosecution becomes apparent because the accused could not sell something on 1.4.69 which he acquired on 1.6.69. This argument is of substance. It is to be noted that the complainant set up a prosecution case that he purchased this truck but no evidence was brought on record which would substantiate the claim of the complainant. Exhibit 4 and 5 series showing the purchase or some spare parts for causing some repairs to the truck could not confer an title on the complainant over the truck as contemplated by the Motor Vehicle Act. Section 31 of the Motor Vehicle Act provides that every transfer of ownership of the vehicle has to be reported to the registering authority by the transferor within 14 days of the transfer and by the transferee within 30 days of the transfer Section 2 prohibit the use of the vehicle unless the sale is registered in accordance with Chapter 3. Section 32 appears under chapter 3. Section 112 is the penal section. The position appears to be this without getting the registration within 30 days of the transfer if the transferee drives the vehicle or causes it to be driven he would on complaint to the Magistrate be liable to be prosecuted and punished under section 22 read with section 112 of the Act. One principle of jurisprudence is that one cannot take advantage of one's own wrong. The complainant on his own showing had not acquired any right and title over the vehicle in question and in that view his allegation is that the vehicle was taken away from his possession without his consent is without foundation inasmuch as his possession is not recognizable in law. This finding is alone sufficient to demolish the prosecution case. As the courts below considered the hypothetical case that even assuming the defence version is correct that the truck was given on bhara still the accused had no right to change the nature of the truck remains to be considered. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman could not lay his finger on evidence to show that the truck was given to the complainant for a specified period. Had there been any such evidence an argument of very weak nature could be advanced. Since there is no such evidence this finding of the Coals below was based on conjecture and is liable to be set aside. 

 Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the opinion is that the prosecution is misconceived in the result, therefore, the Rule is made absolute. The conviction and sentence of the petitioner is hereby set aside.
